findings.issue_text: The top-level OR makes retryCount > 1 independent of method: SMS, allowing the SMS endpoint to delete email or other non-SMS workflow reminders
Retry updates use the stale reminder.retryCount + 1 value, so concurrent handler runs can overwrite each other and undercount attempts
The catch block performs an unprotected database update that can fail, abort the request, and prevent remaining reminders from being processed

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The catch block performs an unprotected database update that can fail, abort the request, and prevent remaining reminders from being processed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a catch block (lines 188-196) that performs a database update without any try-catch protection. If this update fails, it will throw an exception that propagates up and could abort the entire request handler, preventing the remaining reminders in the loop from being processed. The loop iterates over multiple reminders, so a failure in the catch block's database operation for one reminder would stop processing of all subsequent reminders.
